Position: Black to move. FEN: r1bq1rk1/pp3pbp/1Pn3p1/3p4/3B4/1PN5/P3NPPP/2RQKB1R b K - 0 1
Pieces: White: Ke1 Qd1 Rc1 Rh1 Bf1 Bd4 Ne2 Nc3; pawns a2 f2 g2 h2 b3 b6. Black: Kg8 Qd8 Ra8 Rf8 Bg7 Bc8 Nc6; pawns d5 g6 a7 b7 f7 h7.
Material: White is up 3 (pawn units). Phase: 0.95 of non-pawn material left.

Engine (Stockfish, deep search):
- BEST Nxd4: 1...Nxd4(takes bishop) 2.Nxd4(takes knight) Re8+ 3.Be2 Qxb6(takes pawn) 4.Nf3 Qb4 5.Qd2  -> -0.0 (equal)
- ALTERNATIVE axb6: 1...axb6(takes pawn) 2.Bxg7(takes bishop) Kxg7(takes bishop) 3.Qxd5(takes pawn) Qe7 4.Qe4 Qa3 5.Nb5  -> +2.3 (White is better)
- Win-chance cost of the alternative for Black: 20 points (of 100)

Best move Nxd4: knight takes the bishop on d4 (even trade), leaves material en prise on the destination (~3).
Alternative axb6: pawn takes the pawn on b6 (exchange balance +1).

Black can win material now: axb6 wins ~1 (takes pawn)
White threatens (if it were their move): nothing

Imbalances now (us = Black):
- most advanced passed pawn (rank): us 3, them 0
- king's pawn shield: us 3, them 1
- open files next to the king: us 0, them 2
- passed pawns: us 1, them 0
- isolated pawns: us 1, them 0
- doubled pawns: us 0, them 1

Verified concept changes, best line vs alternative (after up to 8 plies, us = Black):
- our forks available: now 0; after best 0; after alternative 3 [favours alternative]
- our trapped enemy pieces: now 0; after best 1; after alternative 0 [favours best]
- our isolated queen pawn: now 1; after best 1; after alternative 0
- our passed pawns: now 1; after best 1; after alternative 0 [favours best]
- our king's pawn shield: now 3; after best 3; after alternative 1 [favours best]

Idea: Trade off the d4 bishop, then use the e-file check against the uncastled king.
Assessment: Equal. Black's lead in development and White's uncastled king make up for the missing material.
Why Nxd4: After 1...Nxd4 2.Nxd4, the check 2...Re8+ forces 3.Be2 and keeps White's king in the centre. Then 3...Qxb6 wins back the b6 pawn with active pieces. The g7 bishop also stays aimed at d4.
Why not axb6: 1...axb6 lets White trade off the g7 bishop with 2.Bxg7. That loosens Black's king, and after 3.Qxd5 Black loses the d5 pawn and gets no compensation.
Concepts: king_safety, initiative, piece_activity
Plan: Attack down the e-file against the stuck king and keep your pieces active.
Difficulty: natural

Idea: Kick the invading queen with tempo and take the half-open g-file.

Why not Ng3: 1...Ng3 grabs at the h1-rook first but leaves White's queen on g7. After 2.Bxf4 Rg8 3.Bg5+, White's queen and bishop hunt Black's exposed king.
Concepts: initiative, king_safety, open_file
